newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up as MGE surges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up as MGE surges.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat prices were higher on Wednesday as MGE spring wheat futures surged and merchants expected farmer selling to pick up.

"We rallied the board like crazy today and I think it probably will start to bring a little wheat out of the country," a Minneapolis-based merchant said. "These are prices that attracted some selling interest last time around."
He added farmers would likely wait to see Thursday's opening calls before deciding whether to sell. A lower call would likely prompt some movement as farmers tried to beat the selloff, he said.
MGE December spring wheat futures closed at $4.17 per bushel, up 16-1/2 cents from Tuesday's close and the highest close since October 15.
But basis levels dropped in parts of North Dakota and Montana in response to compensate for the higher futures values. Dealers cited a lack of demand.
"I just don't think we need the wheat," one Montana dealer said. "There's really nobody in the market for it."
